title: IMP-0015 first slice: provider-neutral model profiles, workload requirements, secret refs, Task Context Contract, refusal telemetry
summary: Operator priority (DEC-0028): make open-weight and abliterated models plug-and-play with neutral routing and neutral context. The existing stdlib router, provider registry, OpenAI-compatible HTTP adapter, keyring code and delegate attachments were extended rather than duplicated. (1) model_profile.py: registry entries may declare a profile (deployment, modalities, open_weights, license, refusal_profile, context_window, revision), with defaults inferred from the adapter; workloads declare hard requirements (deployment, refusal_profile, modalities, open_weights) and soft prefer_* keys. router.select filters on hard keys, orders on soft keys ahead of cost, applies requirements to overrides too, and records the chosen profile on every selection. Nodes (tasks.json 'requirements') and delegate (--require/--prefer) pass them through; reviewers and repairers inherit the subject's requirements. Unknown keys or values fail loudly. Without requirements, routing is unchanged. (2) secret_refs.py: secrets://<provider>/<profile> resolved from AGENT_OS_SECRET_* env vars or the OS keyring; status never returns values; an entry's secret_ref never falls back to a vendor key. (3) context_contract.py: one rendered prompt for every provider, with inputs fenced through the shared delegate.fence_document; safety-relevant facts cannot be omitted (ContextLaunderingError) and every omission is listed. (4) refusal.py: deterministic taxonomy for contract-failed answers, recorded by delegate to <home>/refusals.jsonl and summarized by `orchestrate refusals`. (5) `orchestrate model-add` previews, then with --write adds, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint entry to the machine-local registry; inline role only; never overwrites without --force. The OpenAI-compatible adapter gained options.system. No paid compute, no model calls, no protected-path changes.
